units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: Late to this, Kestrel here. Lab on the fourth floor of a building with frosted windows, so I can't see the ground or anything else. My view is a fire extinguisher and a poster about centrifuge safety. Honestly this thread has been my window this week. Crane, what does the city actually look like from sixty metres?

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: Forecourt clerk. I can see the ground perfectly well, it's the bit with chewing gum on it. Past the forecourt lights there's the bypass and then a field, and at night that field might as well be the sea.

units.author: lh_crane_halvard
units.text: Student: like someone spilled a jar of orange beads and then started sweeping them toward the river. The ring road is a loop of white going one way and red the other. From up here you can't hear any of it, so it's like watching a city on mute. Thank you all for posting. It's been a better week up here for it.

units.author: lh_wren_nights
units.text: There's a yard between the camper and the trees. Somebody banks a fire out there before they turn in, and by about this time it's down to a low orange glow. You can see it from the desk if you lean a little to the left. Past the fire is where the ground stops.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Wren, I'm going to say this kindly: this isn't funny. People on this forum are tired and alone and reading in the dark, and some of them work in exactly the kind of place you're describing. If it's fiction, label it. If it's something else, please talk to someone about it in daylight.

units.author: lh_crane_halvard
units.text: Wren, I started this for cab views and coffee. I'm not the mod and I'm not telling anyone what to post, but this one has got under my skin a bit, sat up here with nothing below me. Where is it you work, if you don't mind me asking?

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: oh love I don't like this one, I've read it twice on my break at the depot and I've gone and sat with my back to the wall where I can see the door, which is silly because it's a bus depot and the only thing out there is the number 9 with its lights on, but I'd rather you wrote about your tea or your shift than about somebody else's fire

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: One small thing, Wren. Your profile says Kestrel Isles. It's half past ten in the morning there right now. So whose night are you describing? I'm not accusing you of anything, I'm just a producer, and producers notice when the clock on a story is wrong.

units.author: lh_wren_nights
units.text: Not mine, like I said. There are five bunks in the cabin across the yard, two each side and one under the window. Someone always lies awake listening to the generator. They count the beats of the exhaust because it's something to count, and because it means the lights are still on.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Since this has wandered toward sleep, a few things that actually help day sleepers: keep the bedroom cold, seventeen or eighteen degrees; eat a light meal before bed, not a fry-up; no screens for the last half hour; and anchor one meal at the same clock time every day, even on days off. The body clock wants a fixed point more than it wants darkness.

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Dmitra's list is the one occupational health hands out, minus the fry-up rule, which is the one everybody ignores. My own addition: foam earplugs and a sign on the front door saying 'night worker asleep, parcels next door please'. It saved my sanity and my neighbour now gets all my post. Back to it.

units.author: lh_wren_nights
units.text: The fixed meal thing works. Porridge at seven in the evening, whatever day it is. Blind down, fan on. I'm on the second night of a run so I'm a bit hollow, but it's helping. Thank you.

units.author: lh_wren_nights
units.text: You stop seeing the screen after a while and start seeing past it. Whatever's outside the window becomes the thing you're really watching. You learn exactly where the ground ought to be, and when it goes dark you wait for it to come back.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Crane, 'a city on mute' is going on the staff-room whiteboard, if that's all right with you. The tunnel's the opposite: all noise, no view. One of our lads has started whistling as he goes down it so the far end knows he's coming. It's mostly the same three notes.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Read the whole thread on the bus. Underground you learn the ground is the only thing you can trust, and it's also the bit that'll have you if you stop respecting it. Up top our town's had its streetlights off two nights running. Put that in its own thread.

units.title: Row K, camera 3
units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Log, for anyone keeping count. 01:30 patrolled row K, nil found. 02:10 monitor 3 showed a shape at the fence end of row K, by the last lamp. Walked out with the torch, nil found. 02:35 back in the gatehouse, kettle on. Monitor 3 again, same place, not moving. Hang on, the camera's

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: dockguard? you've left us on a cliffhanger mate. hope it's a fox. hope it's a fox with a parking ticket. post when you can, I'm on until six and I'll be refreshing between pallets

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Most likely he got called to the gate or the radio, which is what guards do. A post that ends mid-sentence is usually a phone going into a pocket. Still, it would be good to hear back once his shift ends.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: he's a careful poster and he'll be back when his shift lets him. Please don't fill the gap with guesses in the meantime. Glass of water, everyone, and eyes on your own monitors.

units.title: Streetlights out, people in doorways
units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: End of shift. Bus came over the top of the hill and the whole town was dark, every streetlight, second night running. Not a power cut, the houses had lights. Just the street. And people were standing in their doorways with the hall light behind them, looking out. Not talking. Driver slowed right down. Nobody said anything on the bus.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: If the streetlights failed and the houses didn't, that's a street-lighting circuit, which is separate from the domestic supply. People in doorways at half four is the stranger part. Shift change at the pit? People waiting for lifts?

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Some of it, aye. Pit bus goes at five. Not all of them were pit folk though. Old Mrs Haig doesn't wait for anyone. I didn't say it was strange. Just that they were stood there.

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: When our streetlights went last winter people did the same, came to the door to look. I think it's what you do. You check that the dark is the same dark as yesterday's. Back to it.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: There's an old novel in which a whole village comes to its doors on the night the mill stops, because the silence wakes them. I always took it for exaggeration. Perhaps it was reportage.

units.title: Small wins thread
units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Small wins thread, because we need one. Mine: Biscuit the beagle went home today and did a full-body wag at the door, and I didn't cry, much. And Pepper the collie ate her whole breakfast without me sitting next to her, first time in a week. Yours?

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: Small win: a man rang to complain and by the end he'd told me about his tomatoes and thanked me. Nothing got fixed, but he went away happier. Also the pan pipes have been replaced by a harp, which is a lateral move at best.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: Supervisor's comments were mostly nice!! 'Clear and well argued' on page four. I have printed that sentence and stuck it to the centrifuge where I can see it at three in the morning.

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: The glasses man came back. Thanked me, put them on, read the price of a pie, took them off, put them back in the crisp tub and left. I think he's decided they live here now. I've labelled the tub.

units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: Small win: Mr Okafor, who hasn't said much since his stroke, sang the whole of a hymn tonight while I was bringing his cocoa. All four verses, every word. Then he went back to not speaking and patted my hand. I'll take it. I'll take it for a week.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Control fell asleep on the radio and I got through a whole patrol without one 'status check, over'. Also found a two-pound coin in the trolley bay. Net worth up, morale up, van nowhere to be seen. Best night in a fortnight.

units.title: The lines
units.author: hollow_signal

edit.text: Some of us said, a long time ago, that the lights along the coast would go out. Now count the nights. I'm not going to spell it out for people who would rather laugh... but watch which way the faults are moving. Toward the water. Always toward the water. And then out across it.

units.text: Some of us said, a long time ago, that the lights along the coast would go out. Now count the nights. I'm not going to spell it out for people who would rather laugh... but watch which way the faults are moving. Toward the water. Always toward the water.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Source? The co-op fault map is public. The faults are on coastal circuits because coastal circuits are where the salt and the exposed lines are. That's the boring version, and it has the advantage of being written down before the fact, by people with ladders.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: hollow, you've been asked before to post only what you can stand behind. This stays up because it isn't hurting anyone yet, but no follow-ups hinting at secrets, please. Company on the night shift, not campfire stories.

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: The council has now written to say the Rope Walk collection is delayed 'due to power interruptions affecting the depot'. The depot's lorries run on diesel. I asked the man on the telephone what the lorries need electricity for and he said 'the gate'. The gate. Three weeks of bins because of a gate. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Last night: 1033 hPa, wind calm, humidity 68 per cent, minus 4.1 at 03:00, no fog. Very little wind noise on the mast, the quietest night of the year in my log; I could hear the Gilliver foghorn's compressor ticking over across the bay, which I never can. Tess, I've emailed you the hourly table.

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Weyhaven had ours go for twenty minutes at three o'clock. I know because the shop freezer alarm went off under my bedroom. Hysteria, the whole region, everyone carrying on as if the dark were something new. In my day we had candles and we were grateful.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Tess, I've read your cross-check and wx's figures twice, and I owe you a straight answer. I can't explain the two trips on clear nights with corrosion. Residual salt tracking is possible, but I'd expect it to show in damp weather, not in a dry frost. I still think it's equipment rather than anything stranger. But I can't tell you which equipment, and I won't pretend I can.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Bernard, I laughed so hard at 'the gate' that I woke the baby. For the record, the school is open and the head says it's staying open whether the power cooperates or not. They've borrowed a generator for the kitchen, so the dinners are safe.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Brackwater jct lights failed again at 05:50 in last night's cut, came back at 06:20 stuck on red both ways. Queue back to the reservoir lane. Tractor driver got out, looked at it, got back in and drove through. Folk hero.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Thank you, Ferrous. That's fair, and it's more than the office has said to me. For the record, I'm not saying it's anything strange either. I'm saying the breakers think something's there, and I'd like to know what they think it is.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: I've been asked by the office not to post about work on public forums, so I won't, from here on. Tess knows what she's doing. Keep your freezers shut and look after each other.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Update for the cuts thread: ours went at 23:20 last night for about an hour. Pebble was on the windowsill again, ears flat this time, and she growled, which she has never once done in her life. I think it must be a fox. Mill Lane folk, has anyone seen a fox about?

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Tractor driver had the right idea. Half the problems in this region are people sitting about waiting for a light to tell them what to do.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Garvey, thank you for everything you've told us this fortnight. You've been more help than the whole co-op press office put together, and I hope nobody's given you grief for it.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: There is a fox that crosses Tollinby square most nights around now; I've watched it for years from above the shop. Foxes travel a long way in a cold spell, looking for bins that haven't frozen. A cat growling at one through glass is a cat doing her job. Pebble sounds a very good cat.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: For those interested, the society's wiki has an article on the custom, with excerpts from the 1970s oral history tapes. I added a short note this morning that the practice is once again widely observed in Gilliver this month. The earliest written reference we hold is 1883, though families claim it is far older. Nobody has ever recorded a single agreed reason for it.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: When I taught at Lisle the children always drew lamps in the windows in their winter pictures, and I used to correct them gently for putting a light in every window, since most families kept only the one. A small point. I am glad the custom is reviving. It is a kindly one, whatever it was for.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Whoever's walking home round Tollinby at three in the morning wants a taxi, not a bike lamp on a saucer. Just saying what everyone's thinking.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Thank you, that's fascinating. Bike lamp on a saucer installed. My eldest has appointed herself lamp monitor and checks it at bedtime. The six-year-old wanted to know who it's for, and I said 'whoever's walking home', which seemed to satisfy him. Brisk, he says you can borrow it.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: Thank you, Mr Marsh. My mother is on one of your tapes, I believe, though she never said what it was for either. She said you do it and you don't ask. I have kept mine on the sill since I was married, and the window cleaner knows not to move it.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: 'Whoever's walking home' is a fine answer. It's the one I'd give a six-year-old, and also, I find, the one I give myself when I switch mine on above the shop.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Photos received. Can't post them yet because the sender's nervous, but I can describe them: long lens from Harbour Row, four white lights in a line along what must be the yard, one orange low down, and a bright one higher up on the hill, near where the old relay survey put its tower. Why is there a light on the hill? Answer me that.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: What would we expect to see if there were something secret on the hill? Generator noise across the water on a still night, boats to the north landing, contractors' traffic on the harbour log. What we have is a camp of a few people and a fire. A described photograph isn't a photograph.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Since nobody official will say who is out there: I've been told one of the crew is from Weyhaven and has a sister there who's been ringing the Grieve office every day. If she's reading this, I'd love to talk to her. The families deserve answers, and so do the rest of us.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: I have removed the post above. It speculated about a crew member's family, which is exactly what I asked us not to do at the top of this thread. Please don't repost it or paraphrase it. If you have questions for Grieve, the company has an office and a telephone. Thank you.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Finding 3: a light on high ground near the north end would fit a mast for a radio or phone repeater; remote camps often put one up. Finding 4: I can't find a licence for one, but small temporary repeaters don't need one. So this is evidence that someone wants a signal, and of nothing else. I'll say so if that changes.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: The relay survey peg was on the northern knoll. A light 'higher up' at nine kilometres could be a head torch on a slope, a lamp on a generator mast, or a vehicle. A long lens flattens distance badly. If the sender lets you post the image with its metadata, I'll look at it properly. Until then it's a description of a description.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: There's no light on the hill that I've seen, and I've looked at that hill most nights of my life. Four or five down low and the fire. That's all. Long lens or no long lens.

units.author: ex_grieve_corran

edit.text: On Corran we had a work lamp up the slope on a pole. You want to see the edge of the yard from where you sleep. That's all.

units.text: On Corran we had a work lamp up the slope on a pole, so the lads could see the line of the yard from the bunks without getting up. You want to see the edge from where you sleep. That's all it is. I'm not going into the rest of it.

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: I'm sorry to ask, but did it help? The lamp on the slope, I mean. I've been reading about the Holm every night and I keep wondering whether they have one out there. Sorry. You don't have to answer that.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: I taught half the crew on that boat, or their parents. I should like to say, without taking sides on anything, that I'm glad they are going back with proper lights. A crossing in the dark is no small thing, whatever one does or doesn't see from the rail.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Lighting trials went fine last night alongside at Port Ammet. Two complaints from the flats on the quay, one approving look from a gull. Bram, the searchlight has a manual shutter now, so the wheelhouse can douse it coming alongside and not blind your lads at the wall.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Back on nights from tonight. The vessel's been checked, the lighting is a real improvement, and the crew are rested. I won't speculate about what was or wasn't on the slip; I logged what we saw at the time and that log stands. We'll run to the timetable. Logged it, carried on.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Boat's in sight from the Lisle slip... you can see it from halfway across with the new floods, like a little town coming toward you. Everyone on the pier waved, even the ones pretending not to. Ha, anyway. Feels normal. Nearly.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: On the 22:40, which left at 22:40. I've been sarcastic about the welfare review for a fortnight. Got talking to the mate while we waited for the linkspan. She told me what she saw, plainly, no drama, and I'm not going to repeat it because it's hers to tell. I'll just say I won't be calling it 'staff shortages' again.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: One chat on a ferry and he's a believer. She saw a kid in a coat. It's in the other thread. Read it.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: This fits what I'd expected: at least one of the slipway reports was a person. If the lad's account is true, it explains one night in the fog week. It doesn't explain the first report, which came earlier, or the Lisle one. One explanation for one sighting is still progress. We shouldn't stretch it over the others, in either direction.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: A reminder that we are discussing a young person who has not posted here himself. Please do not name him or his family, and please don't guess. If he wishes to speak for himself, he may. Thank you.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Progress, he says. It's a kid, it was always a kid, and the rest is folk scaring each other in the dark. Ferrous, you of all people.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Brisk... I was there, on Lisle. Not in fog, drizzle. I'm not saying what it was. I'm saying it wasn't a Gilliver lad in a coat, because he'd have had to row nine kilometres, and then row back without anyone hearing the oars.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: I'm with Ferrous. One lad, one night, by his own telling. The night ferry crew are not fantasists. I've sat on that boat with them for years and the most dramatic thing I've ever heard Kerris say is that the tea urn needs descaling.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Thanks, Seth, and thanks to the harbour office. I walked the deck at dusk with the floods on. From the wheelhouse you can now see the whole Gilliver slip, right down to the water. That's all any of us asked for. Back on the night run from tonight.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: good to have you back odell. tide tables and the blackout tape both on the counter, and the kettle if you're passing before your shift

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Notice: the Gilliver slip will be coned off from 22:00 to 23:59 tonight to keep the slip head clear for the first night arrival. Please park at the chandlery end of the front. Thank you for your cooperation.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: On tonight with Odell. I checked the floods myself at three this afternoon. If anyone's on the slip tonight, I'll see their face. That's all I'm going to say about it.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Ada, we can feed the Lisle tower from the pier board once the co-op stops tripping it. Until then the genny stays, sorry. Ear defenders are in the chandlery at Gilliver, apparently at a discount if you mention my name, which I've never been asked about.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Night boat's coming in as I type. Floods on, one blast on the horn, lads on the rail. Slip clear. Nobody on the end of it but the harbourmaster in his yellow coat, which is how it should be. Welcome back.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Patrol notes, last night, Gilliver spur, for whoever's keeping the record. Trip 00:22, reclosed. Trip 01:05, locked out. On site by 01:30. Drove the spur end to end, then walked three spans either side of the layby. Frost on everything. Fox prints on the verge. No birds, no branches, conductors clean. I'm starting to dread that layby, and I'm not ashamed to say so.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Been asked by the office to keep work off the forums. Doing as I'm told for once in my life. Tess, go steady, take the second lamp, and don't do that layby on your own.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: garvey's been told to keep quiet, which tells you all you need to know. no more about it on here lads, I'm not losing the only lineman in the Sound who answers a straight question

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: That layby's always been an unfriendly bit of road. My father wouldn't stop his van there, even for a pee. Mind how you go, lass.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Tess, for 00:22 and 01:05: 1033 hPa, calm, humidity 66 to 69 per cent, minus 4 at the station, no fog, visibility 25 km. I've stopped writing 'make of it what you will' under these, because I think by now we've all made of it what we will.

units.title: Prices, cold week
units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Langoustine up a bit, buyers short with the cold keeping boats in. Creels iced to the rope this morning, had to bang them on the gunwale to free them. Holm side flat calm. Could hear the camp generator across the water at five, which I never could before. That's how still it's been.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: bram the ice plant on the north quay's back on soon they reckon, so you'll have ice to sell again instead of ice to bang off. rope and salt in at the chandlery, salt's gone daft with the frost

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Aye, I saw the price. Half the village buying it for their steps. I'll take a coil of the eight mil when you've got it and I'll not pay daft money for salt.

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Good afternoon. I wish you a quiet night for it. When the dam works tape was made, the men knocked off at dusk on account of the cold and the dark, and I think they had the right idea, but I am an old man and fond of my bed. Do keep warm, both of you. Regards, Ned

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Car park gate is locked at ten. Park on the lane if you'll be in after that, and don't block the field gate, the farmer's out at five. Stay on the paths, especially by the sluice. I'll not come looking for anyone in the dark.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Kit for tomorrow, so people can plan round it. Position one: two omnis in blimps on stands, parabolic on a tripod, recorder at -18 dB peaks, 48 kHz, spare batteries inside my coat because the cold eats them. Position two: handheld, foam windshield, headphones. Thermos, two hats. Forecast now says rain from midday, so we may be recording rain. Rain is still a recording.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: If you do record rain, log the start time and any changes in intensity. Rain on foliage is broadband, and you'll want to know which percussive events sit clearly above it. Also, the outflow path floods quickly past the sluice in heavy rain. Wellies, and don't stand on the boards.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so rain is fine, rain is actually great for masking the Tollinby road. I'll have the voice app on with a battery pack, and I've borrowed the binaural head again, it's in a carrier bag so it doesn't get wet, which looks extremely normal on a bus.

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: guys I'm streaming this live from Brackwater tomorrow night, full kit, thermal cam, link in bio, we are going to catch the knocks on camera for the first time ever. actually insane. who's coming, I'll bring the energy drinks

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: No. This is a small, quiet recording session, not a broadcast, and you're on a final warning after last week's ban. If you're at the reservoir, record quietly like everyone else and post the raw file. No streams in this thread, and no thermal footage of other members.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Found the pump. Circulation pump at the ice plant on the north quay, on a timer, 50 Hz motor, mounted on a plinth that sits right on the quay wall. That'll carry into the water lovely. Mystery solved, nothing to see, thanks Hollis.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Good. A plinth-mounted pump coupling into a masonry quay wall would explain both the level and the lack of direction. One question before we close it: did you hear it running while you were there, or only see it?

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Saw it, didn't hear it, the plant was shut up when I went round. Timer box on the wall though, and the cable runs straight to the plinth. It'll be that. That's a pump.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Aw. A little disappointing but very satisfying. Headphones off. I'll still think of it as the caravan fridge, if nobody minds, because a pump on a plinth has no romance at all.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: Morning love, Irena, I've read all this coming off shift and I'll be honest with you all, I used to come home at five and go up those stairs two at a time and never hear a thing, which I said was more worrying if anything, and now I sit in the lobby with my flask and wait for it to get light before I go up, which is daft because the lights are on, but there it is

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Shop notice: torches and batteries back in stock, cost price for residents as before. Flasks too. I've put a chair inside the shop door for anyone who wants to wait for a neighbour before going up. No need to buy anything, just sit. H

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear Lorna, it is not daft. You are welcome to wait for the daylight in my flat; I am up at six and the kettle is always warm. My late husband would have said we are two silly women. Then he would have sat and waited with us. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Mass hysteria from the upper floors, as I've said from the start. Lorna, you're on five, you of all people should know better. I take the stairs every morning to the shop and back and I've never heard a thing. Except the once. Which I'm not discussing.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Lorna, Irena, if you two want, I'll put a notice up asking anyone coming in before daylight to knock for a neighbour. No shame in it. Notes from the last meeting are on the board by the lift, including the bit about the bins, Wendell. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Update for the record. 3 further files, from 7 and 9, daylight, lights on. Step counts per flight: 19, 19, 21. Expected: 19. I am aware that I am the only person in this building who finds this important. I will post a table at the weekend for anyone who wants it.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: ok irena and lorna's dawn club is the most wholesome thing that has ever happened in this building. can i join if i bring croissants. sincerely though, i took the stairs at 1am tonight and they were just stairs. just stairs. weirdly that didn't help

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: I'd join the dawn club but I'm usually still up from the night before (deadlines), so I'll be the one coming down as you're all going up, waving. Sketch of tonight's landing: identical to yesterday's, which I'm choosing to find soothing.

units.title: Notice ref KE/DC/0923: lift maintenance
units.author: dellow_manager
units.text: Kerrow Estates notice ref KE/DC/0923. Residents are advised that the passenger lift will be taken out of service between 10:00 and 13:00 on the next working day for planned maintenance following recent faults. Stair access will be available throughout. Stairwell lighting is fully operational. We thank residents for their patience.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: 'Stair access available throughout.' Yes. Thank you. I am at work so it is fine for me, but for Irena on 7 it is three hours. Irena, I can carry your shopping up the night before if you want. Sorry for spelling.

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Mrs Tollinby, if I may, I have checked under the frost. No lorry. I have, however, counted the bins on Rope Walk still standing at the kerb: thirty-one. I have written to the council again, enclosing the count. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Bernard, news from Weyhaven: ours were collected at six this morning by a lorry I didn't recognise, driven by a lad who didn't know the estate and reversed into the bollard outside the shop. So, progress of a sort.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Bernard, you may call me that, it's better than what my children call me. Thirty-one bins is practically a monument at this point. I hope the council brings flowers when they finally come.

units.title: Brackwater jct. Day whatever.
units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Brackwater jct temp lights. Came back from the cut stuck on red both ways and were still on red at 06:25 when I came through on the second run. Waited six min. Two of us flashed each other and went. Can somebody tell me why a junction with a reservoir lane, a farm gate and a bus stop needs four-way temp lights for a month to dig one hole?

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Because the council loves a cone, lads. Same reason the Tollinby bypass has had a sign saying 'new road layout' for three years. It isn't new. It's just bad.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: The hole is a culvert under the reservoir lane that the council left far too long. It floods in heavy rain and the lane goes under. They're doing it before the rain comes, which is the first sensible thing they've done all year. The lights are a nuisance, I'll grant you.
